<!-- libs/error-codes/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-error-codes

SVTA2070 standardized streaming error codes.

This package is the reference implementation of [SVTA2070: Standardized Error Codes](https://www.svta.org/product/svta2070/). The specification defines one error vocabulary for every video player. Each code is a short integer. The thousands digits identify the category, such as Playback or Network. The last three digits identify the specific error. HTTP response statuses and IAB VAST error codes embed into the scheme at their own values.

## When to use

- Report a playback, network, DRM, or ad error with an SVTA2070 code: `SVTA_BUFFER_APPEND_ERROR`, `SVTA_BAD_LICENSE_REQUEST`
- Map an HTTP response status to an SVTA2070 code: `httpStatusToSvtaErrorCode`
- Map an IAB VAST error code to an SVTA2070 code: `vastErrorToSvtaErrorCode`
- Read the category or the index of a code: `getSvtaErrorCategory`, `getSvtaErrorIndex`

Do not define your own error code list for a player or an analytics pipeline. Open an issue for a condition that the specification does not name.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-error-codes
```

## Usage

Codes are grouped into one catalog per category. Each catalog is an `as const` object, so autocomplete lists the valid members:

```typescript
import assert from "node:assert";
import { getSvtaErrorCategory, SvtaErrorCategory, SvtaPlaybackErrorCode } from "@svta/cml-error-codes";

const code = SvtaPlaybackErrorCode.VIDEO_BUFFER_UNDERRUN;

assert(code === 2001);
assert(getSvtaErrorCategory(code) === SvtaErrorCategory.PLAYBACK);
```

Every code is also an individual constant:

```typescript
import assert from "node:assert";
import { SVTA_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND } from "@svta/cml-error-codes";

assert(SVTA_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND === 3004);
```

### Embed external error codes

HTTP response statuses embed into the Network category. IAB VAST error codes embed into the Advertising category. The four-digit VAST error 1009 (empty VAST response) maps to 7999.

```typescript
import assert from "node:assert";
import { httpStatusToSvtaErrorCode, vastErrorToSvtaErrorCode } from "@svta/cml-error-codes";

assert(httpStatusToSvtaErrorCode(404) === 3404);
assert(vastErrorToSvtaErrorCode(301) === 7301);
assert(vastErrorToSvtaErrorCode(1009) === 7999);
```

The helpers never throw. Out-of-range input returns the unknown code of the target category, 3000 or 7000.

## References

- [SVTA2070: Standardized Error Codes](https://www.svta.org/product/svta2070/)
- [IAB VAST 4.0 §2.3.6.3 Error Codes](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/VAST_4-0_2016-01-21.pdf)

<!-- libs/id3/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-id3

ID3 tag parsing functionality.

## When to use

- Read the ID3 frames in an HLS timed metadata sample or an emsg payload: `getId3Frames`, `Id3Frame`
- Read the PRIV timestamp that HLS uses to map ID3 time to media time: `getId3Timestamp`
- Check that a buffer holds an ID3 tag: `canParseId3`
- Match the ID3 emsg scheme in a DASH event stream: `ID3_SCHEME_ID_URI`

Do not write your own ID3 header, size, or frame parser. Open an issue for a frame type that is missing.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-id3
```

## Usage

```typescript
import { getId3Frames } from "@svta/cml-id3";

// id3Data holds the bytes of one ID3 tag, for example from an HLS timed metadata sample.
function logId3Frames(id3Data: Uint8Array): void {
	for (const frame of getId3Frames(id3Data)) {
		console.log(frame.key, frame.data);
	}
}
```

<!-- libs/id3/config/cml-id3.api.md -->
## API Report File for "@svta/cml-id3"

> Do not edit this file. It is a report generated by [API Extractor](https://api-extractor.com/).

```ts

// @public

};
```

<!-- libs/iso-8601/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-iso-8601

ISO 8601 date/time handling functionality.

## When to use

- Convert a DASH or HLS ISO 8601 duration such as PT1M30S to seconds: `decodeIso8601Duration`
- Format a number of seconds as an ISO 8601 duration: `encodeIso8601Duration`

Do not write your own duration regular expression. Open an issue for a duration form that does not decode.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-iso-8601
```

## Usage

```typescript
import {
	decodeIso8601Duration,
	encodeIso8601Duration,
} from "@svta/cml-iso-8601";

// Encode duration
const encoded = encodeIso8601Duration(3661);
// encoded === 'PT1H1M1S'

// Decode duration
const decoded = decodeIso8601Duration("PT1H1M1S");
// decoded === 3661
```

<!-- libs/iso-8601/config/cml-iso-8601.api.md -->
## API Report File for "@svta/cml-iso-8601"

> Do not edit this file. It is a report generated by [API Extractor](https://api-extractor.com/).

```ts

// @public
export function decodeIso8601Duration(isoDuration: string): number;

// @public
export function encodeIso8601Duration(duration: number): string;

// (No @packageDocumentation comment for this package)

```

<!-- libs/iso-bmff/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-iso-bmff

ISO Base Media File Format (ISO BMFF) parsing.

## When to use

- Parse the boxes of an init or media segment, with full content for the box types that you need: `readIsoBoxes`, `findIsoBox`, `filterIsoBoxes`, `traverseIsoBoxes`
- Read the track timescale, codec, or default sample duration from moov and moof: `readMdhd`, `readStsd`, `readTfhd`, `readTrun`
- Read the base media decode time, the segment index, or event messages: `readTfdt`, `readSidx`, `readEmsg`
- Read pssh and encryption boxes: `readPssh`, `readTenc`, `readSchm`
- Write boxes to a ReadableStream: `createIsoBoxReadableStream`, `IsoBoxReadableStream`
- Write or patch boxes, such as inserting emsg or rewriting tfdt: `writeIsoBoxes`, `writeIsoBox`, `writeEmsg`, `writeTfdt`
- Read or write a box type that the package does not name: `IsoBoxReadView`, `IsoBoxWriteView`

Do not write your own box parser, box walker, or box writer. Open an issue for a box that is missing.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-iso-bmff
```

## Usage

- [Reading boxes](https://cml.svta.org/llms/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md) - Parse ISO BMFF boxes from a buffer
- [Writing boxes](https://cml.svta.org/llms/iso-bmff/docs/writing-boxes.md) - Write boxes to byte arrays or streams
- [Utilities](https://cml.svta.org/llms/iso-bmff/docs/utilities.md) - Traverse boxes and type guards

<!-- libs/iso-bmff/docs/reading-boxes.md -->
---
title: Reading Boxes
description: Parse ISO BMFF boxes from a buffer
---

# Reading Boxes

The `readIsoBoxes` function reads boxes from a buffer and returns an array of parsed boxes. By default, the function reads only the box header. To parse the content of a box, provide a reader function for that box type.

> [!NOTE]
> The function parses container boxes automatically, so they do not need a reader function. The `CONTAINERS` constant lists all known container types.

## Using default config

If tree shaking is not a concern, use `defaultReaderConfig()`. It returns a configuration with every available reader:

```typescript
import { defaultReaderConfig, readIsoBoxes } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const buffer = await fetch("https://example.com/bbb.mp4").then((r) =>
	r.arrayBuffer(),
);

const boxes = readIsoBoxes(buffer, defaultReaderConfig());
```

## Using specific readers

For optimal bundle size with tree shaking, import only the readers you need:

```typescript
import { readFtyp, readIsoBoxes } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const buffer = await fetch("https://example.com/bbb.mp4").then((r) =>
	r.arrayBuffer(),
);

const boxes = readIsoBoxes(buffer, {
	readers: {
		ftyp: readFtyp,
	},
});
```

<!-- libs/iso-bmff/docs/utilities.md -->
---
title: Utilities
description: Traversing boxes and type guards
---

# Utilities

## Traversing boxes

The `traverseIsoBoxes` function traverses box iterators and returns a generator of boxes. It takes an iterable of boxes and two optional arguments: depth-first traversal and maximum depth. By default, the function traverses depth-first with a maximum depth of infinity. A maximum depth of 0 traverses only the root boxes.

```typescript
import { readIsoBoxes, traverseIsoBoxes } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const boxes = readIsoBoxes(buffer);

for (const box of traverseIsoBoxes(boxes)) {
	console.log(box.type);
}
```

## Type guards

The library provides type guards that check whether a box is a container box or a full box. These guards narrow the type of a box in TypeScript.

`isContainer` checks whether a box is a container box.

```typescript
import { isContainer, type IsoBox } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const box: IsoBox = { type: "meta", version: 0, flags: 0, boxes: [] };
const container = isContainer(box);
```

`isFullBox` checks whether a box is a full box.

```typescript
import { isFullBox } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const box = { type: "meta", version: 1, flags: 0 };
const fullBox = isFullBox(box);
```

<!-- libs/iso-bmff/docs/writing-boxes.md -->
---
title: Writing Boxes
description: Write boxes to byte arrays or streams
---

# Writing Boxes

The `writeIsoBoxes` function writes boxes. It takes an array of streamable items and returns an array of `Uint8Array`s. Streamable items include:

- Raw box objects, such as `{ type: 'ftyp', majorBrand: 'isom', minorVersion: 1, compatibleBrands: ['isom'] }`
- ArrayBufferViews such as `Uint8Array` and `DataView`, and the box structures that `readIsoBoxes` returns. Those structures implement the `ArrayBufferView` interface.

If you provide raw box objects, also provide a configuration object that names the writers for those box types.

> [!NOTE]
> The function writes container boxes automatically, so they do not need a writer function. The `CONTAINERS` constant lists all known container types.

## Using default config

If tree shaking is not a concern, use `defaultWriterConfig()`. It returns a configuration with every available writer:

```typescript
import { defaultWriterConfig, writeIsoBoxes, type IsoBoxStreamable } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const boxes: IsoBoxStreamable[] = [
	{
		type: "ftyp",
		majorBrand: "isom",
		minorVersion: 1,
		compatibleBrands: ["isom"],
	},
	{
		type: "mdat",
		data: new Uint8Array([
			102, 105, 114, 115, 116, 115, 101, 99, 111, 110, 100, 116, 104, 105, 114,
			100,
		]),
	},
];

const byteArrays = writeIsoBoxes(boxes, defaultWriterConfig());

for (const byteArray of byteArrays) {
	sourceBuffer.appendBuffer(byteArray);
	// wait for updateend event
}
```

## Using specific writers

For optimal bundle size with tree shaking, import only the writers you need:

```typescript
import { writeFtyp, writeIsoBoxes, writeMdat, type IsoBoxStreamable } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const boxes: IsoBoxStreamable[] = [
	{
		type: "ftyp",
		majorBrand: "isom",
		minorVersion: 1,
		compatibleBrands: ["isom"],
	},
	new Uint8Array([
		0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x14, 0x66, 0x74, 0x79, 0x70, 0x69, 0x73, 0x6f, 0x6d,
		0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x69, 0x73, 0x6f, 0x6d,
	]),
	{
		type: "mdat",
		data: new Uint8Array([
			102, 105, 114, 115, 116, 115, 101, 99, 111, 110, 100, 116, 104, 105, 114,
			100,
		]),
	},
];

const byteArrays = writeIsoBoxes(boxes, {
	writers: {
		ftyp: writeFtyp,
		mdat: writeMdat,
	},
});

for (const byteArray of byteArrays) {
	sourceBuffer.appendBuffer(byteArray);
	// wait for updateend event
}
```

## Streaming boxes

The `createIsoBoxReadableStream` function writes boxes to a readable stream. It supports both the default config and specific writers:

```typescript
import {
	createIsoBoxReadableStream,
	defaultWriterConfig,
	type IsoBoxStreamable,
} from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const boxes: IsoBoxStreamable[] = [
	{
		type: "ftyp",
		majorBrand: "isom",
		minorVersion: 1,
		compatibleBrands: ["isom"],
	},
	{
		type: "mdat",
		data: new Uint8Array([
			102, 105, 114, 115, 116, 115, 101, 99, 111, 110, 100, 116, 104, 105, 114,
			100,
		]),
	},
];

const readableStream = createIsoBoxReadableStream(boxes, defaultWriterConfig());

const stream = await transport.createBidirectionalStream();
readableStream.pipeTo(stream.writable);
```

## Type safety

In TypeScript, cast raw box objects to a box type for type safety. There are two ways. The first way uses a box type from the library:

```typescript
import type { FileTypeBox } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const box: FileTypeBox = {
	type: "ftyp",
	majorBrand: "isom",
	minorVersion: 1,
	compatibleBrands: ["isom"],
};
```

The second way uses the `as const` operator on the `type` property:

```typescript
const box = {
	type: "ftyp" as const,
	majorBrand: "isom",
	minorVersion: 1,
	compatibleBrands: ["isom"],
};
```

You can also get a box type from `IsoBoxMap` with the box's FourCC:

```typescript
import type { IsoBoxMap } from "@svta/cml-iso-bmff";

const box: IsoBoxMap["ftyp"] = {
	type: "ftyp",
	majorBrand: "isom",
	minorVersion: 1,
	compatibleBrands: ["isom"],
};
```

<!-- libs/request/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-request

Common Media Request and Response types.

## When to use

- Type a segment, manifest, or license request that a player passes through a plugin: `CommonMediaRequest`
- Type the response that comes back, with timing and headers: `CommonMediaResponse`
- Type the function that performs a request, so that fetch or XMLHttpRequest can implement it: `Requester`
- Intercept requests and responses, for example to add CMCD or to read CMSD: `RequestInterceptor`, `ResponseInterceptor`

Do not define your own request and response types for a plugin interface. Open an issue for a field that is missing.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-request
```

## Usage

```typescript
import type { CommonMediaRequest, CommonMediaResponse, Requester } from "@svta/cml-request";

// A requester adapts an HTTP client to the common request and response types.
const fetchRequester: Requester = async (request: CommonMediaRequest): Promise<CommonMediaResponse> => {
	const response = await fetch(request.url, { method: request.method, headers: request.headers });
	return {
		request,
		url: response.url,
		status: response.status,
		statusText: response.statusText,
	};
};

// Pass fetchRequester to a component that accepts a Requester, and call it with a request like this one.
const request: CommonMediaRequest = {
	url: "https://example.com/video/segment_001.m4s",
	method: "GET",
};
```

<!-- libs/structured-field-values/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-structured-field-values

RFC8941 Structured Field Values implementation.

## When to use

- Decode an RFC 8941 header such as CMCD, CMSD, or Priority into items, lists, or dictionaries: `decodeSfDict`, `decodeSfList`, `decodeSfItem`
- Encode a dictionary, a list, or an item as a structured field header: `encodeSfDict`, `encodeSfList`, `encodeSfItem`
- Represent an item with parameters or a token: `SfItem`, `SfToken`

Do not write your own structured field tokenizer or serializer. Open an issue for an RFC 8941 form that fails to parse.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-structured-field-values
```

## Usage

```typescript
import { encodeSfDict } from "@svta/cml-structured-field-values";

const dict = encodeSfDict({
	a: 1,
	b: false,
	c: "x",
	d: Symbol.for("y"),
	e: new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]),
});

console.log(dict);
// a=1, b=?0, c="x", d=y, e=:AQID:
```

<!-- libs/throughput/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-throughput

Throughput estimation functionality.

## When to use

- Estimate throughput from segment downloads with an exponentially weighted moving average: `EwmaEstimator`
- Estimate throughput with a harmonic mean, an arithmetic mean, or a zero-lag EWMA: `HarmonicMeanEstimator`, `ArithmeticMeanEstimator`, `ZlemaEstimator`
- Implement a custom estimator behind the shared interface: `ThroughputEstimator`
- Tune the fast and slow half-lives of the EWMA: `EwmaEstimatorOptions`

Do not write your own EWMA or harmonic mean for bandwidth estimation. Open an issue for an estimator type that is missing.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-throughput
```

## Usage

```typescript
import { EwmaEstimator } from "@svta/cml-throughput";

const estimator = new EwmaEstimator({ fastHalfLife: 2, slowHalfLife: 5 });

// 500 bps
estimator.sample({
	startTime: 0,
	encodedBodySize: 125,
	duration: 2000,
});

// 250 bps
estimator.sample({
	startTime: 2000,
	encodedBodySize: 125,
	duration: 4000,
});

console.log(estimator.getEstimate());
// 285
```

## Samples

A sample needs an `encodedBodySize` above 0 and a `duration` above 0. The estimators ignore every other sample, and the estimate does not change.

A player can pass `PerformanceResourceTiming` entries as samples. For a cross-origin segment, the browser decides whether the entry has a body size:

| Browser | Body size of a cross-origin response |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome | Exposed when the response has a `Timing-Allow-Origin` header for the page origin. Chrome plans the Firefox rule for version 158. |
| Firefox 129 and later | Exposed when the request used CORS. A `no-cors` request reports 0, even with the header. |
| Safari | 0 for every cross-origin response. |

An entry with a body size of 0 is ignored, so the estimate does not change. The byte count of the loader works in every browser. Build the sample from that count when the player has it.

<!-- libs/utils/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-utils

Common utility functions for media processing.

## When to use

- Convert between hex, base64, UUID strings, and byte arrays: `hexToArrayBuffer`, `arrayBufferToHex`, `arrayBufferToUuid`, `uuidToArrayBuffer`, `decodeBase64`, `encodeBase64`
- Encode or decode UTF-8 and UTF-16 text: `encodeText`, `decodeText`, `Encoding`
- Resolve a base URL or make a URL relative to another URL: `getBaseUrl`, `urlToRelativePath`
- Compute bandwidth in bits per second from a byte count and a duration: `getBandwidthBps`
- Unescape HTML entities in a manifest or a caption string: `unescapeHtml`
- Generate a UUID for a session or a content id: `uuid`

Do not write your own hex, base64, or UUID conversion. Open an issue for a conversion that is missing.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-utils
```

## Usage

```typescript
import {
	stringToUint16,
	hexToArrayBuffer,
	decodeBase64,
	arrayBufferToUuid,
	arrayBufferToHex,
	unescapeHtml,
} from "@svta/cml-utils";

// Unescape HTML entities
console.log(unescapeHtml("&quot;&lt;Hello&amp;World&gt;&quot;"));
// "<Hello&World>"

// Convert string to Uint16Array
console.log(stringToUint16("hello world"));
// Uint16Array(11) [104, 101, 108, 108, 111, 32, 119, 111, 114, 108, 100]

// Convert hex string to ArrayBuffer
const hex = "a0564af760c2d94b9610c7ae70d5d970";
const arrayBuffer = hexToArrayBuffer(hex);
console.log(new Uint8Array(arrayBuffer));
// Uint8Array(16) [160, 86, 74, 247, 96, 194, 217, 75, 150, 16, 199, 174, 112, 213, 217, 112]

// Decode base64
console.log(decodeBase64("SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ="));
// Uint8Array(11) [72, 101, 108, 108, 111, 32, 87, 111, 114, 108, 100]

// Convert ArrayBuffer to UUID
const data = new Uint8Array([
	160, 86, 74, 247, 96, 194, 217, 75, 150, 16, 199, 174, 112, 213, 217, 112,
]);
console.log(arrayBufferToUuid(data.buffer));
// a0564af7-60c2-d94b-9610-c7ae70d5d970

// Convert ArrayBuffer to hex string
console.log(arrayBufferToHex(data.buffer));
// a0564af760c2d94b9610c7ae70d5d970
```

<!-- libs/webvtt/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-webvtt

WebVTT parsing and rendering functionality.

## When to use

- Parse a WebVTT file or segment into cues, regions, and styles: `parseWebVtt`, `WebVttParser`
- Parse WebVTT chunks as the bytes arrive from a stream: `WebVttTransformStream`, `WebVttTransformer`
- Read the X-TIMESTAMP-MAP header of an HLS WebVTT segment: `WebVttParser`, `TimestampMap`
- Create native VTTCue and VTTRegion objects from parsed cues: `toVttCue`, `toVttRegion`
- Build cues and regions without a browser, for tests or servers: `createWebVttCue`, `createWebVttRegion`

Do not write your own WebVTT tokenizer, cue timing parser, or timestamp map handling. Open an issue for a cue setting that is missing.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-webvtt
```

## Usage

```typescript
import { parseWebVtt } from "@svta/cml-webvtt";

const vtt = `WEBVTT\n\nREGION\nid:test\n\nSTYLE\n::cue {}\n\nCUE_1\n00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:35.000\nWebVTT Sample\n`;

const { cues, errors, regions, styles } = await parseWebVtt(vtt);

console.log(cues[0].id, cues[0].text);
// CUE_1 WebVTT Sample
console.log(errors.length, regions[0].id, styles.length);
// 0 test 1
```

<!-- libs/xml/README.md -->
# @svta/cml-xml

XML parsing utilities.

## When to use

- Parse a DASH MPD or another XML document into a node tree: `parseXml`
- Find elements by name anywhere in the tree: `getElementsByName`
- Serialize a node tree back to an XML string: `serializeXml`
- Keep whitespace or comments, or start the parse at an offset: `XmlParseOptions`

Do not write your own XML tokenizer for manifests. Open an issue for an XML form that fails to parse.

## Installation

```bash
npm i @svta/cml-xml
```

## Usage

```typescript
import { parseXml } from "@svta/cml-xml";

const obj = parseXml(
	`<root>
		<child>text</child>
		<ns:tag>content</ns:tag>
	</root>`
);

const root = obj.childNodes[0];
console.log(root.nodeName);
// root
console.log(root.childNodes[0].nodeName, root.childNodes[0].childNodes[0].nodeValue);
// child text
console.log(root.childNodes[1].nodeName, root.childNodes[1].prefix, root.childNodes[1].localName);
// ns:tag ns tag
```

```ts
import { XmlNode } from '@svta/cml-utils';

export function getElementsByName(node: XmlNode, name: string, found?: XmlNode[]): XmlNode[];

// @public
export function parseXml(input: string, options?: XmlParseOptions): XmlNode;

// @public
export function serializeXml(xml: XmlNode): string;

export { XmlNode }

// @public
export type XmlParseOptions = {
    pos?: number;
    keepWhitespace?: boolean;
    keepComments?: boolean;
    includeParentElement?: boolean;
};

// (No @packageDocumentation comment for this package)
```
